run.change_description: fix(utils/body,validator): normalize Content-Type media type for case-insensitive matching

summary.intent: Normalize Content-Type media-type matching so `parseBody()` and `validator()` accept mixed/upper-case media types (e.g. `Application/JSON`), per honojs/hono#5060.
summary.issue_fit: Met for the stated acceptance criteria: `parseBody()` and `validator('json'|'form')` now match mixed-case media types via lowercase comparison/`/i` regexes, and `bufferToFormData` only lowercases the segment before `;` so multipart boundaries survive untouched. All new tests for these criteria pass. The chosen implementation path introduces an unrelated regression (see finding below) not covered by any acceptance criterion or new test.
summary.coverage: All 6 changed files read in full (diff + surrounding context). Traced `parseFormData`'s new body-cache interaction against `HonoRequest#cachedBody` in src/request.ts (unchanged by this diff). Ran the affected and adjacent test files with the clone's vitest at the reviewed head. Reproduced a caching regression with an esbuild-bundled scratch script (run with node, per the run's execution allowance) and confirmed it does not occur against the merge-base implementation.
check_details: `./node_modules/.bin/vitest --run --project main --coverage.enabled=false src/utils/body.test.ts src/utils/buffer.test.ts` at 5226d416: 50 passed, 1 skipped.

`./node_modules/.bin/vitest --run --project main --coverage.enabled=false src/request.test.ts` at 5226d416: 38 passed (file unchanged by this diff; passes because none of its cases call `formData()` before `parseBody()`).

Scratch reproduction (esbuild --bundle --platform=node --format=esm, run with node) at 5226d416: calling `c.req.formData()` then `c.req.parseBody()` on the same request throws for multipart and returns corrupted data for urlencoded; the identical scenario against the merge-base's `parseBody` (9728702) succeeds correctly both times.

findings.title: Reuse cached formData in parseFormData instead of rebuilding it from a stale Content-Type
findings.trigger: `c.req.formData()` (directly, or by any code that reads it first, e.g. a middleware) runs before `c.req.parseBody()` on the same `multipart/form-data` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` request.
findings.impact: `parseFormData` now always calls `request.arrayBuffer()` first. When only `bodyCache.formData` is already cached, `HonoRequest#cachedBody`'s fallback rebuilds bytes via `new Response(cachedFormData).arrayBuffer()`, which the Fetch spec always re-serializes with a brand-new random multipart boundary, while `parseFormData` still passes the original, now-stale `Content-Type` header (old boundary) to `bufferToFormData`. For multipart requests this throws `Failed to parse body as FormData.` out of `parseBody()`; for urlencoded requests it silently returns corrupted data (a `------formdata-undici-...` boundary line as the sole key) instead of `{message: 'hello'}`. Confirmed by direct execution; the same sequence against the merge-base's `parseFormData` (which calls `request.formData()` directly and hits `#cachedBody`'s already-cached short-circuit) succeeds correctly.
findings.change: In `parseFormData` (src/utils/body.ts:121-139), check `request.bodyCache.formData` first and `await`/reuse it when present, mirroring the pattern `validator('form')` already uses for the same cache (src/validator/validator.ts:115-121), before falling back to `arrayBuffer()` + `bufferToFormData()`.

observations.fact: Codecov (PR packet §6) reports src/utils/body.ts patch coverage at 75% (3 missing lines) and src/utils/buffer.ts at 50% (1 missing line); the missing branches are exactly parseFormData's new bodyCache-population path, consistent with the untested regression above.

`request.bodyCache.formData = formDataPromise as unknown as FormData` stores a pending Promise under a field typed `FormData`; this mirrors `#cachedBody`'s own existing convention of storing an unresolved promise under a resolved-value-typed key, so it is not a new type-safety regression.
